meta.purpose: Absolute health targets — what a healthy number IS, independent of what soksak happens to do today. Kept apart from budgets.json on purpose: budgets are baseline x headroom, which detects regression but cannot detect an absolute defect, because the baseline is whatever the defect already produced. Recorded consequence: budgets.json derives t5_idle.cpu.avg max 60 from a 46.4 baseline, so the gate certifies half a core burned at rest.
meta.rule: A target is never invented. Each entry carries the measurement or the arithmetic it was derived from, and the command that reproduces it. A target is never widened to make a run pass — if it cannot be met, the next bottleneck is located by measurement.
meta.gate: check-budgets.mjs reports a miss as BELOW_TARGET and exits 3. Exit 3 means: no regression, but not green either.

measured.deliveryUnit: ~1030 B. Derived from every recorded t1 run: writtenBytesDelta/ackSentDelta = 5127..5231 while FLOW_ACK_SIZE=5000 (soksak-plugin-terminal-xterm/src/terminal.ts:25). The ack fires at the first cumulative >= 5000, so the observed value is unit*ceil(5000/unit): unit=8192 would give 8192, unit~1030 gives 5150. Reproduce: jq over scripts/perf/results/*.json.
measured.costIsPerCrossing: t1_ansi 4.49 vs t1_plain 4.58 = 2% apart. A stream dense with escape sequences costs the same as plain text, so the cost is attached to the number of crossings, not to the bytes.
measured.fastPathThreshold: tauri channel.rs:39 MAX_RAW_DIRECT_EXECUTE_THRESHOLD = 1024, guarded by `bytes.len() < 1024` — a ~1030 B chunk misses the direct path and pays a script eval plus an ipc:// fetch round trip.

t1_plain.mbps / t1_ansi.mbps.arithmetic: A 64 KiB batch replaces 65536/1030 = 63.6 crossings with one. If crossings were the whole cost, 4.58 x 63.6 = 291 MB/s. Real paths never recover the full factor, so the target is set at 100 — 34% of the projected ceiling.
t1_plain.mbps / t1_ansi.mbps.onMiss: Do not widen this number. Locate the next bottleneck by measurement and record it here.

progress.rigWithdrawn: These two runs were taken on a throwaway com.soksak.perf identity that has since been removed from the tree — it was invented to route around a keychain authorization prompt rather than asking for it, which was the wrong call. The numbers stand and are kept as evidence, but reproducing them needs a release-profile build of an existing identity: `make build` with TAURI_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY set, or `tauri build --config frameworks/tauri/tauri.build-debug.conf.json` and approving the keychain prompt the new signature raises.
progress.measured: t1_plain 40.83 MB/s, t1_ansi 33.65. Against the same rig one build earlier (20260726-001819, delivery still per read) that is 8.4 and 7.83; against the original recorded baseline, 4.58 on the dev profile.
progress.deliveryUnit: writtenBytesDelta/ackSentDelta = 64,601 B, i.e. exactly DELIVERY_BATCH_BYTES. The unit is doing what the contract says.
progress.stillShort: 40.83 against a target of 100. The constraint moved: writeCbLagMs accumulated 10,059 ms across a 2,449 ms run, so several writes are in flight at once and the backlog now lives inside the terminal's parse rather than in the crossing — which is where it belongs, and which is the next thing to measure. rafFrames 134 over 2.449 s is 55 fps, so the renderer is keeping up. Next step is to attribute inside xterm (parse vs render vs addon hooks) before changing anything.
progress.notRegressed: t2 median 1 ms, p95 2, max 3 — the interactive path took nothing from the batch hold, which is the property DELIVERY_MIN_HOLD_BYTES exists to keep.

t5_idle.cpu.avg.measured: 30s CPU-time delta on the running dev instance, 2 windows, zero input (2026-07-25): WebContent 82658 = 8.00%, soksak-dev 82541 = 4.17%, GPU 82625 = 3.90%, and the three idle siblings 82626/82627/82749 = 0.03/0.03/0.00%. Reproduce: difference `ps -o time=` over the attributed pid set across a fixed window.
t5_idle.cpu.avg.arithmetic: The sibling renderers prove the floor: a WebKit process with nothing to do costs ~0.0% of a core. Idle is by definition the state where there is no work, so the healthy number is near zero. 5% across the whole app group is generous headroom, not a compromise.
t5_idle.cpu.avg.onMiss: Attribute per process before changing anything — a whole-group sum hides which process is guilty (see W-M2).

notDerivedYet.t1_plain.cpu.avg: No honest absolute number exists yet. Today's 100.0 measures a main thread saturated by crossings at 4.58 MB/s; the CPU cost of a healthy path can only be measured once the delivery unit is fixed. Derive it from the run that first meets t1_plain.mbps >= 100, and record the derivation here.
notDerivedYet.t6_memory.rssMb: RSS is the wrong instrument — macOS compresses and swaps under pressure and RSS excludes exactly that, so the metric stops rising when pressure starts. Replace with physical footprint (W-M3), re-baseline under a stated window population, then derive.
notDerivedYet.t2.medianMs: 1 ms is good, but the measurement point excludes paint (driver.mjs records 'socket RPC/paint excluded'). A key-to-paint target needs the scenario that measures it (s14) to exist first.
